title: Elliott Smith: The Artist
description: From Portland basements to the Oscars stage: the whispered songs, the albums and the life of Elliott Smith.

cards.prompt: What was Elliott Smith's birth name?
cards.details: He started going by Elliott as a teenager, and the name stuck.

cards.prompt: In which US city was Elliott Smith born, in 1969?
cards.details: He grew up mainly in Texas before moving to Oregon as a teenager.

cards.prompt: Elliott Smith is most closely associated with which Pacific Northwest city?
cards.details: He went to high school and made his first records there. Portland landmarks show up in his songs.

cards.prompt: Which loud Portland rock band was Elliott Smith in before going solo?
cards.details: Much heavier than his solo work. He wrote quiet acoustic songs on the side, which became his real calling.

cards.prompt: Who co-founded Heatmiser with Elliott Smith?
cards.details: The two had met at college and shared songwriting duties in the band.

cards.prompt: What is Elliott Smith's 1994 debut solo album?
cards.details: Recorded at home on a four-track. He reportedly didn't intend it for release at first.

cards.prompt: Which Olympia, Washington indie label released his second and third albums?
cards.details: A key label of the '90s Northwest underground, also home to Sleater-Kinney.

cards.prompt: What is the title of Elliott Smith's 1995 second album?
cards.details: A self-titled record of stark, dark acoustic songs that built his cult following.

cards.prompt: What is Elliott Smith's 1997 third album, titled after a Kierkegaard book?
cards.details: Many fans' favourite. See the Either/Or set for the full story.

cards.prompt: Which 1997 film used several Elliott Smith songs and launched him to wider fame?
cards.details: Director Gus Van Sant was a fan and a fellow Portland resident.

cards.prompt: Which Elliott Smith song from Good Will Hunting was nominated for an Oscar?
cards.details: He performed it at the 1998 Academy Awards in a white suit. It lost to Titanic's "My Heart Will Go On".

cards.prompt: Who directed Good Will Hunting?
cards.details: A Portland-based filmmaker who championed Smith's music.

cards.prompt: What is Elliott Smith's 1998 major-label debut album?
cards.details: Lusher and more Beatles-inspired, with piano, horns and strings, but still unmistakably him.

cards.prompt: Which XO single has a waltz rhythm and a number in its title?
cards.details: One of his best-known songs, built on a woozy 3/4 rhythm.

cards.prompt: Which band was Elliott Smith's biggest musical influence and lifelong obsession?
cards.details: You can hear it in his melodies and harmonies, especially on XO and Figure 8.

cards.prompt: Smith's soft vocals were often layered using which recording technique?
cards.details: Singing each line twice and stacking them gives his voice that ghostly, close-up feel.

cards.prompt: What is Elliott Smith's 2000 album, the last released in his lifetime?
cards.details: His most ambitious, full-band record. Parts were recorded at Abbey Road, a dream for a Beatles fan.

cards.prompt: The Figure 8 cover was photographed in front of a mural in which city, now a fan memorial?
cards.details: The wall on Sunset Boulevard in Silver Lake became a pilgrimage site, covered in messages from fans.

cards.prompt: In what year did Elliott Smith die, aged 34?
cards.details: He died in Los Angeles while working on his next album. The exact circumstances remain unresolved.

cards.prompt: What is the posthumous album, released in 2004, that he had been working on?
cards.answer: From a Basement on the Hill
cards.details: Completed by family and collaborators from his unfinished recordings.

cards.prompt: Which 2007 posthumous double album gathered unreleased songs from his Kill Rock Stars years?
cards.details: Full of songs as good as anything he officially released.
